synopsis: Great Britain remains governed by the Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008, as amended, imposing general essential health and safety requirements and conformity obligations; SI 2026/867 amendments take effect on 20 January 2027 [f2216, f2218, f2217]. The 8 August 2026 notice designated the EN 474:2022 earth-moving machinery family, giving a presumption of conformity, although the booklet flags uncertainty about the notice number [f15244, f15246]. Designation does not turn EN 474 into an automatic-braking performance matrix, and the survey found no dedicated Great Britain off-road automatic-braking test regime [f15245, f2219]. Planning must account for Britain's parallel declaration path and separate standards-designation calendar, rather than assuming one declaration covers both Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where EU product law applies [f15496, f15494]. HSE's cross-industry 2025/26 figures record 126 worker deaths, including 24 from moving vehicles—the second-largest category behind falls from height at 31—but these are not earthmover-, quarry- or mine-specific figures [f3146, f3147]. Undated quarry guidance attributes 40% of accidents and 60% of deaths to transport, while the 2024/25 sources present a tension between an approximately 16% moving-vehicle fatality share and a vendor-reported 14 of 124 deaths [f3206, f3207, f3149, f3152].
